what: The lines of each installed executor root that state the review ladder, at the checkpoint Part C began on and as Part C leaves them.

.claude/skills/dotln-executor/SKILL.md: Every execution and fix runs its independent reviews as a ladder with an end, before the complete validation run and only after implementation or repair and its write-backs are complete, never as early scouts. Round 1: three fresh independent `dotln-worker` reviewers over the whole diff against the merge base, each given the current order and diff with nonoverlapping briefs. The criteria adversary seeks concrete counterexamples, failed acceptance criteria and missing regression tests; exclude design cleanup. The design improver seeks simpler structure, coupling, error handling and six-month maintainability; exclude criterion verdicts and adversarial test design.

Fix or record every finding; transfer a finding to the responsible reviewer instead of reviewing it twice. Round 2, the recheck: each reviewer whose findings were fixed confirms those fixes, then reviews the whole current change against the base again, resumed where the host keeps it (Claude `SendMessage`) or as a fresh worker given its prior report; a new finding is admitted only when it breaks an acceptance criterion or a behavior `main` had, and any other new finding is recorded in the handoff, not fixed. Round 3, the last: only when round 2's fixes changed code again, one combined worker carrying the three briefs reads the delta since round 2's reviewed tree under the same rule. After round 3 no reviewer runs in this execution or repair: you judge the remaining delta. Skip a round, and say so, when the fixes before it touch only comments, documentation, formatting, test names or regenerated files. Finish the ladder before the selected runs and run no reviewer after they pass; you and an earlier run's reviewers cannot stand in for a round. Each round's report lives in `docs/control/local/reviews/WO-NNN/round-<N>-<kind>.md`, a repair's under `repair-<n>/`: the helper writes its own, and you record an `Agent` worker's returned text there with `npm run worker -- record --kind <kind> --round <N> --from <file> [--host <host> --model <model> --effort <level>] [--tree <tree>]`, naming what ran and the tree it reviewed. Add handoff.md line `self-review: found N; fixed N; recorded N; rounds R; unreviewed M lines (<reason>)` with every round's counts and reports.

.claude/skills/dotln-executor/SKILL.md: Every execution runs its independent reviews as a ladder with an end, before the complete validation run and only after implementation and its write-backs are complete, never as early scouts. The order's `**Review ladder:**` header line sizes round 1, which reads the whole diff against the merge base: `full`, or no line, is three fresh independent `dotln-worker` reviewers, each given the current order and diff with nonoverlapping briefs; `combined` is one worker carrying the three briefs (`npm run worker -- review --kind combined --round 1`); `paired` is those three reviewers and one combined worker on the same tree, all launched before any fix and none given another's report. In every round a finding blocks when it names the acceptance criterion it fails and an input the kit's writers or an author's ordinary text produce, or a leak (a copy, a broken link or a wrong pass admitted), or behavior `main` had with the probe that shows it; anything else is reported as a recorded finding.

The criteria adversary seeks concrete counterexamples, failed acceptance criteria and missing regression tests; exclude design cleanup. The design improver seeks simpler structure, coupling, error handling and six-month maintainability; exclude criterion verdicts and adversarial test design.

Judge each finding before you act on it, and write the judgment in the round's decision: the writer that produces the input the finding names, or that none does; whether the failure is open (something wrong is admitted) or closed (something valid is refused); and what the fix costs. A reviewer's label is the reviewer's claim; the judgment is yours. Fix an open failure, and a closed failure on a real writer's input. Record a closed failure on an input no writer produces, with no code. Prefer a parsed structure to a new scanner of source text. Transfer a finding to the responsible reviewer instead of reviewing it twice. After a `paired` round 1, first record each distinct finding in that decision's `roundFindings` array, then fix the union under this rule; an entry holds `id`, `finders` (among `criteria`, `design`, `consistency` and `combined`), `class` (`criterion`: it fails an acceptance criterion on a supported input or breaks behavior `main` had; `lesser`: a real defect a gate or a final review would meet; `improvement`; `none`: no writer produces the input, or the finding is wrong) and `disposition` (`fixed` or `recorded`).

Round 2, the recheck: each reviewer whose findings were fixed confirms those fixes, then reviews the whole current change against the base again, resumed where the host keeps it (Claude `SendMessage`) or as a fresh worker given its prior report; a new finding is admitted only when it breaks an acceptance criterion or a behavior `main` had, and any other new finding is recorded in the handoff, not fixed. Round 3, the last: only when round 2's fixes changed code again, one combined worker carrying the three briefs reads the delta since round 2's reviewed tree under the same rule. After round 3 no reviewer runs in this execution or repair: you judge the remaining delta. Skip a round, and say so, when the fixes before it touch only comments, documentation, formatting, test names or regenerated files. Finish the ladder before the selected runs and run no reviewer after they pass; you and an earlier run's reviewers cannot stand in for a round. A fix dispatch (`resume: fix`) answers its report and runs no ladder: repair the failing case and the class the failed report names, redesign only where recorded evidence shows the larger change is the better solution, then run one combined review over the repair's change since the tree that report judged (`npm run worker -- review --kind combined --since <tree>`, or one `dotln-worker` given the three briefs and that diff) under the same rules, and no other round.
